recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中多為帶顆粒的骨髓系前驅細胞：箭頭所指為核圓、有核旁淡染區與細紫紅顆粒的前骨髓細胞（promyelocyte），周圍還有數個含顆粒的骨髓細胞與較成熟的後骨髓細胞，顯示 G-CSF 刺激下的骨髓系增生與左移。
features: Predominance of granulated myeloid precursors: promyelocytes, myelocytes and metamyelocytes
Arrowed promyelocyte: large cell with round eccentric nucleus, fine chromatin, perinuclear clear zone and abundant azurophilic granules
Myelocytes with round-to-oval nuclei, more condensed chromatin and granular pink-purple cytoplasm
Occasional band/metamyelocyte with indented nucleus; one cell with dark condensed chromatin (possible erythroid precursor)
No Auer rods, no blasts clusters and no dysplastic hypogranulation evident; stain precipitate in background
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a predominance of granulocytic precursors across the maturation spectrum, including large promyelocytes with round eccentric nuclei, a perinuclear clear zone and abundant azurophilic granules (arrow), myelocytes, and occasional metamyelocytes/band forms. A cell with dark condensed chromatin may represent an erythroid precursor. No Auer rods, blast aggregates, or obvious granulocytic dysplasia are identified, and background stain precipitate is present. Findings are consistent with a left-shifted myeloid hyperplasia secondary to G-CSF therapy; correlation with the recent G-CSF administration and a blast count on a well-spread area is recommended to exclude residual or relapsed leukemia.

ddx.vs: APL shows sheets of abnormal hypergranular promyelocytes with bilobed nuclei and faggot cells with arrested maturation, whereas here maturation to myelocytes and metamyelocytes is preserved.
CML shows myeloid hyperplasia with myelocyte bulge, basophilia and small hypolobated megakaryocytes with BCR::ABL1 fusion, and lacks a G-CSF history.
Regenerating marrow also shows synchronous left-shifted myelopoiesis and is separated mainly by clinical timing, with both lacking a blast excess.
ALL relapse shows agranular lymphoblasts with high N:C ratio and fine chromatin, whereas these cells are granulated maturing myeloid forms.
